lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to break a problem into smaller procedures, build a solution from them, and refactor repeated code into a procedure.
Decomposition means breaking a big problem into smaller ones.
A house is a square plus a roof; a street is houses in a row.
Write and test the small procedures first (square, roof), then a bigger one (house) that calls them.
Once house works, you can use it without thinking about its details.
Abstraction hides complexity behind a simple name.
Refactoring is improving the structure of code without changing what it does — like replacing copy-pasted blocks with a procedure.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
